title: Family sues city, police over shooting death of man mistaken as thief
article: The family of a homeless man shot dead by Vancouver police last year have filed a civil suit against the city and police force, their lawyer says.

Michael Hubbard, 58, was shot once and killed on March 20 after being mistaken by police for a robbery suspect. Police claimed the man came after them with a box-cutter that he refused to drop; Mr. Hubbard's family said he was a peace-loving man who used an X-acto knife to create cards for relatives.

The case was mired with controversy from the start, when a witness claimed he videotaped the incident on his cellphone only to have police delete the file. Police also later admitted they'd mistaken Mr. Hubbard for the thief.

One week after the shooting, the family had pledged to file a lawsuit against the Vancouver Police Department. A writ of summons was only filed this Monday, on behalf of the man's two daughters by the Pivot Legal Society, an agency advocating for Vancouver's homeless and marginalized.

"The beneficiaries are making a claim for wrongful death," said Pivot lawyer Nina Purewal, alleging the police used "excessive force" in the shooting of Mr. Hubbard. The Illinois women are seeking an unspecified amount in damages from the city force.
The shooting is being investigated by the Abbotsford Police Department.
